cues.text: Born Hildebrand to a family of humble standing in Tuscany, Gregory VII spent decades as the power behind several popes before he was himself acclaimed pope by the shouting of the Roman crowd at Pope Alexander II's funeral.
He devoted his pontificate to a single, relentless purpose: freeing the Church from the control of kings and nobles who bought and sold bishoprics as if they were parcels of land.

His standoff with the German Emperor Henry IV produced one of the most famous scenes of the Middle Ages, when the humbled emperor stood barefoot in the snow outside the castle of Canossa begging absolution.
Driven from Rome in his final year by Henry's armies, Gregory died in exile at Salerno, reportedly saying, 'I have loved righteousness and hated iniquity; therefore I die in exile.'
